high.title: Luhut Gives Strong Signal That Customs Functions Will Be Taken Over by DSI
high.summary: National Economic Council Chairman Luhut signals major restructuring of Indonesia's customs operations, with export duties potentially transferred from Customs to new state-owned export company DSI using AI-based systems. This represents a fundamental shift in Indonesia's trade administration that could significantly impact export processes and government revenue collection.

high.title: Danantara Responds to S&P and Moody's on Single Export Gateway Risks via DSI
high.summary: Major credit rating agencies S&P and Moody's warn that Indonesia's new centralized export policy through DSI could harm exports, reduce government revenue, and negatively impact the country's credit rating prospects. This policy poses significant risks to Indonesia's economic outlook and investor sentiment.

high.title: Purbaya Holds Data on 10 Palm Oil Companies Manipulating Exports, Sold Cheap to Singapore
high.summary: Finance Minister reveals that all 10 largest palm oil exporters are engaged in under-invoicing practices, causing estimated losses of US$84 million from just a small sample. This massive fraud in Indonesia's key export sector threatens government revenues and highlights systemic issues in trade oversight.

high.title: FTSE Russell Kicks Out 4 Indonesian Stocks, Here Are Their Violations
high.summary: FTSE Russell removes four Indonesian stocks from its Global Equity Index Series due to high shareholding concentration and free float violations. This delisting affects foreign investment flows and contributes to continued pressure on Indonesian stock market performance.

high.title: Luhut on Rupiah and IHSG Bleeding: Indonesia Won't Collapse
high.summary: Despite significant pressure on the rupiah and IHSG from capital outflows, Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain strong with fiscal deficit at only 0.93% of GDP. Senior official assures that Indonesia has never defaulted and maintains confidence in economic resilience despite current market volatility.

high.title: IHSG Closes Higher at Start of Week
high.summary: Indonesian stock index IHSG closed up 0.72% to 6,206.34 points after volatile trading, providing some relief after recent heavy losses. The recovery comes amid ongoing concerns about foreign outflows and market reforms.

medium.title: 13th Month Salary for Civil Servants to be Disbursed in June, Here's the Amount
medium.summary: Indonesian civil servants will receive their 13th month salary bonus starting in June 2026 as part of government efforts to boost purchasing power and economic growth. This fiscal stimulus measure affects millions of government employees and their spending patterns.

medium.title: 27 Countries Queue to Borrow from World Bank Due to Middle East War
medium.summary: Twenty-seven countries are seeking emergency funding from the World Bank following the Middle East conflict that began in February 2026. This global financial stress could affect international funding availability and borrowing costs for emerging markets including Indonesia.

medium.title: Prabowo Agrees Family Office to be Built in Bali, Place for World Conglomerate Money
medium.summary: President Prabowo approves establishment of family office around Bali's International Financial Center, with legislation expected to pass on June 4, 2026. This initiative aims to attract wealthy international investors and position Indonesia as a regional financial hub.

medium.title: BEI Welcomes 7 Million New Investors
medium.summary: Indonesia Stock Exchange reports 7.4 million new investors from January to May 20, 2026, bringing total investors to 27.4 million. This strong growth in retail participation demonstrates continued confidence in Indonesian capital markets despite recent volatility.

medium.title: Trade Minister Speaks Out on Alfamart Indomaret Closure in Lombok
medium.summary: Trade Minister clarifies that closure of several Alfamart and Indomaret stores in Central Lombok is due to licensing issues and regional spatial planning compliance, not policy changes. The situation reflects ongoing regulatory challenges for retail expansion in Indonesia.

medium.title: Trade Minister Opens Up About Trade Tariff Certainty with US
medium.summary: Following US Supreme Court cancellation of previous trade agreement, the US has imposed temporary 10% tariffs for 150 days while conducting Section 301 trade investigations on Indonesian products. This uncertainty affects Indonesian exporters and bilateral trade relations.
